screening_results.reason: None of the exclusion criteria (E1-E3) apply. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy adult sample), I4 (reports task-related activations). Inclusion criterion not met: I2 — participants viewed emotional photos but were not instructed to regulate or reappraise their emotions.

Excluded because the abstract reports only a depressed patient sample with no healthy adult/control group (E2). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation via introspection), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met/demonstrated: I3 (no healthy control group reported).

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study where participants received a short mindfulness instruction to regulate emotional responses to negative pictures; includes healthy adult groups (24 individuals, 22 controls) and reports task-related brain activations (prefrontal, amygdala, insula). No exclusion criteria apply.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy adult sample), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criterion not met: I2 (does not test emotion regulation/reappraisal of emotional responses to pictures; task involves introspection/self-reflection rather than instructed reappraisal of responses to stimuli).

Excluded for E3: the study is an empathy/perspective-taking task predicting others' emotions without instructions to amplify/attenuate participants' own emotional responses. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I2 (no explicit reappraisal/regulation instruction), I3 (healthy adult sample not specified).

Abstract reports task-based fMRI with passive viewing and effortful attempts to regulate emotional responses (meets I1, I2, I4). The abstract does not specify participant ages or whether a healthy adult control group was included, so inclusion criterion I3 is not demonstrated. Because the age/sample information is insufficient from the abstract, include for full-text review to determine adult healthy sample eligibility.

Task-based fMRI study of younger and older adults using reappraisal (and distraction) to regulate responses to negative stimuli; reports MVPA and univariate brain activation results. Meets I1–I4; no exclusion criteria apparent.

Abstract describes a task-based rt-fMRI study where healthy adult participants used a cognitive emotion-regulation strategy (‘reality check’) to down-regulate amygdala responses to emotional pictures and reports task-related brain activation/connectivity results. No exclusion criteria met.

The abstract investigates reappraisal and acceptance of negative self-beliefs in social anxiety disorder, indicating an emotion-regulation task relevant to the review (I2). However, the abstract does not explicitly state task-based fMRI methods, presence of a healthy control group, or that task-related brain activation results are reported (I1, I3, I4 not demonstrated). Because key inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed from the abstract, include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI study explicitly examines cognitive up-regulation (engaging/increasing) of positive-social emotions with a self-referential first-person perspective, reports fMRI activation and connectivity, and involves human participants (no patient-only sample reported). Meets inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are indicated in the abstract.

Excluded per E2: study includes only adolescent girls (ages 9–16) and does not include a healthy adult sample. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation/reappraisal task), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criterion not met/not demonstrated: I3 (healthy adult group).

EXCLUDED because E2: study focuses on adolescents and does not include a healthy adult sample. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (examines neural correlates of emotion regulation). Inclusion criteria not met or not demonstrated in abstract: I1 (task-based fMRI not explicitly stated), I3 (no healthy adult group), I4 (task-related activation results not explicitly reported).

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy adult participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criterion not met: I2 — the study uses reappraisal of monetary incentives in a motor/performance task, not reappraisal of emotional responses to pictures or an explicit emotion-regulation task addressing the review objective.

Abstract lacks sufficient information to determine whether this is a task-based fMRI reappraisal study or includes healthy controls. No exclusion criteria are clearly met, but inclusion criteria (task-based fMRI, reappraisal emotion-regulation task, healthy adult sample, task-related activation) are not demonstrated in the abstract; include for full-text review.

Excluded (E2): No healthy adult sample — participants were children (~10 years). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (investigates automatic emotion regulation) and I4 (reports task-related brain activation via MEG). Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (not task-based fMRI; uses MEG) and I3 (no healthy adult group).

Task-based fMRI study using an explicit reappraisal task with emotionally evocative pictures; reports task-related brain activations (amygdala, insula, temporal, parahippocampal regions); involves human participants (healthy adults characterized by Machiavellian traits). All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Abstract reports investigation of neural substrates of emotion regulation in women with PMDD, indicating an emotion-regulation task with reported brain activation; however it does not specify use of fMRI, reappraisal instructions, or whether healthy controls were included. Insufficient detail to confirm all inclusion criteria, so include for full-text review.

Inclusion criteria I1-I4 are met (task-based fMRI; reappraisal/acceptance task; healthy adult sample; reports task-related brain activation). However, the study used idiographic autobiographical scripts/negative self-beliefs, not pictures. The meta-analysis objective specifically targets regulation of emotional responses to pictures, so this study does not address the review objective and is excluded.

Task-based fMRI in 42 participants using attentional deployment to explicitly increase/decrease negative affect while viewing unpleasant images (an explicit emotion regulation goal). Reports task-related brain activation and connectivity (amygdala, fronto-parietal, precuneus). Sample appears to be healthy adults. Attentional deployment is an emotion regulation strategy, so the study meets inclusion for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI study examining reappraisal (emotion regulation) and reporting neural activation/pattern-information results. The abstract does not explicitly state the participant population (healthy adults) so include for full-text review to confirm I3.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study using a cognitive reappraisal paradigm in regular marijuana users and matched nonusing healthy controls, with task-related neural activation and connectivity results reported. All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Abstract lacks sufficient methodological detail to confirm inclusion criteria: it discusses volitional emotion regulation and reappraisal-related substrates in anxiety/depression, which aligns with the review objective, but does not explicitly state this is a task-based fMRI study, whether healthy control participants are included, or that task-related activation results are reported. Therefore include for full-text review to determine eligibility.

Abstract reports emotion processing and regulation in OCD, includes unaffected siblings and unrelated healthy control participants (so a healthy adult sample is present). However the abstract does not specify use of reappraisal, pictures, or explicit task-based fMRI activation reporting. Insufficient detail to determine if reappraisal and task-based activation criteria are met — include for full-text review.

EXCLUDED because study used resting-state fMRI and questionnaires (ERQ) rather than a task-based reappraisal paradigm; it includes healthy controls (I3) but does not meet I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation/reappraisal task), or I4 (reports task-related activation). No exclusion criteria met.

EXCLUDED because the healthy control group is age-matched adolescents (not adults), so the study lacks a healthy adult sample (E2). The abstract does satisfy I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performed reappraisal/detachment to downregulate emotion), and I4 (reports task-related brain activation). It does not meet I3 (no healthy adult group).

Study is resting-state fMRI, not a task-based emotion regulation/reappraisal study and does not report task-related activations. Includes healthy control group. Therefore it fails I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation/reappraisal task), and I4 (task-related activation results).

The study used resting-state fMRI and graph-theory analyses of network organization; it does not describe a task-based emotion regulation or reappraisal paradigm, nor report task-related activations. Inclusion met: I3 (healthy adult sample). Inclusion not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation/reappraisal task), I4 (task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria (E1-E3) are met.

Task-based fMRI study of reappraisal to aversive social images in 78 adolescents/young adults, reporting task-related activations (amygdala, fusiform, temporal-occipital). Participants appear to be healthy; meets I1–I4 and no exclusion criteria are met.

No exclusion criteria from the list are met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performed an emotion-regulation task), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not met or not demonstrated: I3 (healthy adult sample not explicitly reported). Primary reason for exclusion: study regulates emotions elicited by recollected autobiographical memories (internal stimuli), not emotional pictures as required by the review objective; therefore it does not address the review’s focus on reappraisal of responses to pictures.

No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Inclusion met: I3 (healthy adult sample). Inclusions NOT met / not demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study; resting-state only), I2 (no task in which participants regulated emotions; dispositional ERQ only), I4 (no task-related activation reported). Therefore excluded for failing required task-based emotion regulation and task-activation criteria.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study using reappraisal of angry faces (explicit emotion regulation), reports task-related activations (vmPFC, vlPFC–amygdala coupling), and appears to involve healthy adult participants. No exclusion criteria are evident.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study assessing generation of alternative appraisals for anger-evoking events (reappraisal), and reports task-related brain activations. The sample health status is not specified in the abstract, so eligibility for healthy adult inclusion is uncertain; include for full-text review to confirm participant characteristics.

Abstract lacks key details: it does not state that task-based fMRI was used, that participants performed an explicit reappraisal/emotion-regulation task, the participant sample (healthy adults) or that task-related brain activation results are reported. Because inclusion criteria (I1–I4) cannot be confirmed from the abstract, include for full-text review to determine eligibility.

The abstract describes a task-based fMRI study (n=60) in healthy adults that used a reappraisal paradigm asking participants to reduce negative affect to pictures and reports task-related neural activation and predictive analyses. All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Include for full-text review: EEG and fMRI were simultaneously recorded from 20 human subjects during emotion processing and regulation tasks, reporting cortical activation/network results. Abstract does not specify reappraisal strategy or use of pictures, so full text needed to confirm alignment with meta-analysis focus.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in healthy young adults who reappraised negative pictures to down-regulate affect; reports task-related brain activations and correlations. Meets I1, I2, I3, and I4; no exclusion criteria met.

No task-based emotion regulation paradigm: this is a resting-state connectivity study. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met or not demonstrated: I1 (not task-based; resting-state fMRI), I2 (no emotion regulation/reappraisal task), I4 (no task-related activation reported). I3 (healthy control group) not demonstrated in abstract.

E2 met: study includes only juvenile (male) participants and healthy controls are not adults. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (human reappraisal task), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (no healthy adult sample).

No task-based fMRI or task-related activation reported: this is a structural MRI (voxel-based morphometry) study correlating trait reappraisal/suppression with gray matter volume. Includes healthy adult sample (I3) but does not meet I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation/reappraisal task), or I4 (task-related brain activation results). No exclusion criteria met.

Task-based fMRI study examining implicit and explicit emotion regulation (attention-shift and reflective appraisal) during viewing of emotional faces/pictures; reports task-related brain activations. Abstract implies healthy adult sample (no patient population mentioned). Fits reappraisal/instructional appraisal inclusion. Recommend full-text for confirmation of participant health/age and task instructions.

Study does not investigate intentional emotion regulation/reappraisal of emotional pictures. Inclusion met: I3 (healthy adult sample). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI not clearly reported in abstract), I2 (no reappraisal/emotion regulation task described), I4 (task-related brain activation results not reported in abstract). No exclusion criteria (E1-E3) were explicitly met.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI film-based emotion regulation task in a population-derived sample of adolescents/young adults (healthy participants implied) and reports task-related neural activation (including PFC and amygdala). However, it does not specify use of reappraisal or use of pictures (films used), so inclusion for full-text review is warranted to clarify strategy and stimulus modality.

Excluding because the abstract does not report an instructed emotion regulation/reappraisal task (I2 not met): it examines implicit modulation via facial-expression primes rather than explicit reappraisal. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy adults), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria met (none applied).

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study (two samples including fMRI) where participants used reappraisal to regulate incidental emotions; reports task-related brain activation in prefrontal and cingulate regions; involves human participants (healthy adult samples implied). Thus meets I1-I4 and no exclusion criteria are met.

Task-based fMRI with a cognitive emotion regulation task, includes healthy control group, and reports task-related brain activation. Abstract does not specify that regulation was reappraisal or that stimuli were pictures, so eligibility for the meta-analysis is uncertain — include for full-text review.

Included for full-text review: task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal of aversive pictures; reports task-related brain activation (LPFC feedback reduced amygdala response and altered connectivity). Abstract does not explicitly state whether participants were healthy adults, so include to confirm I3.

No evidence participants were instructed to regulate or reappraise emotions (I2 not demonstrated). Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy control group present), I4 (reports task-related activation/connectivity). No exclusion criteria clearly met (none).

EXCLUDED because inclusion criterion I2 (emotion regulation/reappraisal task) is not met: the study used a mood induction procedure (positive faces and autobiographical recall) rather than instructing participants to reappraise or explicitly regulate their emotional responses. Inclusion criteria met: I1, I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I2. No exclusion criteria (E1-E3) clearly apply.

Abstract reports structural (anatomical) MRI and trait measures of reappraisal in healthy females; it is not a task-based fMRI study, does not describe participants performing an emotion regulation/reappraisal task, and reports no task-related brain activation. Therefore it meets inclusion I3 (healthy adults) but fails I1, I2, and I4. No exclusion criteria are met.

Task-based fMRI study of human participants (ages 6–23) using an explicit reappraisal (distancing) emotion-regulation task; includes healthy participants including adults; reports task-related brain activation (amygdala, vmPFC, vlPFC). Meets inclusion criteria I1, I2, I3, I4. No exclusion criteria met.

Excluded because the study used an oddball attention task with negative distractors but did not instruct participants to regulate or reappraise their emotional responses. Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy control group), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (no emotion regulation/reappraisal task described).

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI battery including two volitional reappraisal tasks and reports task-related activations, satisfying I1, I2, and I4. Participant population (healthy adults) not explicitly stated, so I3 is uncertain. No exclusion criteria apparent. Include for full-text to confirm participant characteristics.

EXCLUDED: no task-based fMRI or emotion regulation/reappraisal task; reports resting-state connectivity and voxel-based morphometry without task-related activations. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (includes healthy controls). Inclusion IDs not met / not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation/reappraisal task), I4 (task-related brain activation results).

Study is a task-based pharmaco-fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants that uses a reappraisal (emotion regulation) task with negative pictures and reports task-related brain activation and connectivity results. No exclusion criteria are met.

Excluded because the task provokes and measures aggressive responding without any instruction to regulate or reappraise emotions (I2 not met). Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy adults), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria met (none applied).

E3 met: study is a perspective-taking/debate task without instruction to regulate participants' own emotional responses; does not involve reappraisal of emotional reactions to pictures. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy adult participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met: I2 (no emotion regulation/reappraisal task described).

This is a structural VBM study, not a task-based fMRI investigation of emotion regulation/reappraisal. It does not report task-related activation or any reappraisal/emotion-regulation task. Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met or not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation/reappraisal task), I4 (task-related activation results); I3 (healthy adult sample) not demonstrated in abstract.

Task-based fMRI study examining reappraisal (up- and down-regulation) of emotional responses to angry faces; includes both patients with depression and healthy control participants; reports task-related neural activation results. Therefore it meets I1–I4 and no exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study where participants (GAD, PD, and healthy controls) reappraised or maintained emotional responses to negative images, reporting PFC activation differences. Meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract indicates a task-based fMRI study examining brain activation and connectivity during emotion regulation, but does not specify use of reappraisal, stimuli (pictures), or whether healthy control group is included. Insufficient information to exclude; include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI study where participants explicitly used Reappraisal (and Compassion) to regulate their own emotional responses to film clips; includes healthy adult practitioners and reports task-related brain activation. Although stimuli are film clips rather than static pictures, the abstract meets the review inclusion criteria and provides sufficient info for full-text review.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a cognitive reappraisal task with pictures. It includes healthy adult groups (younger and older adults) and reports task-related brain activation and connectivity. No exclusion criteria are met.

Excluded (E2): No healthy adult sample — participants are adolescent inpatients and the study used resting-state fMRI. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (not task-based fMRI; resting-state), I2 (no emotion regulation/reappraisal task), I3 (no healthy adult group), I4 (no task-related activation reported).

Excluded because the study used odorant (olfactory) stimuli rather than pictures required by the review objective. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (explicit emotion regulation instruction to decrease emotion), I3 (healthy adult sample), I4 (reports task-related brain activations). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: does not address the review objective of regulation of emotional responses to pictures (stimulus modality mismatch).

Excluded because the study used highly arousing film clips (videos), not pictures, so it does not meet the meta-analysis objective of regulation of responses to pictures. Abstract shows task-based fMRI (I1), an explicit reappraisal/up–down regulation task (I2), and reports task-related activation/results (I4). Inclusion criterion I3 (healthy adult sample) is not demonstrated in the abstract. No exclusion criteria (E1–E3) are clearly met.

EXCLUDED: No explicit emotion regulation or reappraisal task is described (I2 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not demonstrated: I2 (no reappraisal/regulation instructions), I3 (healthy adult sample not explicitly stated). No exclusion criteria (E1–E3) are clearly met.

Task-based fMRI study where human participants used reappraisal (reinterpretation) to downregulate emotional responses to pictures; reports task-related neural activation (amygdala, PFC, parietal). Abstract implies healthy participants (no patient sample mentioned). Meets all inclusion criteria; no exclusion criteria met.

E2 met: abstract describes fMRI reactivity in depressed patients undergoing CBT but gives no indication of a healthy adult control group. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI) and I4 (task-related neural reactivity reported). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I2 (no evidence of an emotion regulation/reappraisal task) and I3 (no healthy control group reported).

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study using a creative cognitive reappraisal emotion-regulation task with behavioral and imaging results (amygdala, hippocampus, striatum). It meets I1, I2, and I4. The abstract does not explicitly state inclusion of healthy adult participants (I3 not demonstrated), so include for full-text review to confirm participant sample.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I3 (healthy adult participants). Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study; uses arterial spin labeling at rest), I2 (no emotion regulation/reappraisal task—resting-state), I4 (no task-related activation reported).

Excluded because the study does not involve participants actively regulating their emotional responses (reappraisal); it is a passive viewing/emotion-perception study. Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (includes healthy adult controls), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criterion not met: I2 (no emotion regulation/reappraisal task reported).

Abstract examines amygdala reactivity and brain connectivity in depressed and healthy control groups but does not specify an emotion regulation/reappraisal task. It clearly includes healthy adults (controls). Insufficient information in abstract to confirm reappraisal task, so include for full-text review to determine I1/I2/I4.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants used reappraisal-based emotion regulation), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I3 (abstract does not explicitly state inclusion of a healthy adult sample), and importantly the study does not address the review objective of regulating emotional responses to pictures—it examines reappraisal during financial decision-making, not picture-based regulation.

Meets inclusion: task-based fMRI with within-subject design (I1), healthy adult sample of women (I3), explicit instruction to cognitively control urges toward pictured food (explicit regulation/reappraisal-like task; I2), and reports task-related brain activation (I4). Although the regulation target is craving rather than classic emotion, the abstract describes an explicit regulation goal; include for full-text review.

Explicit cognitive reappraisal task (Reappraise vs Look-Negative) using aversive images during task-based fMRI in 49 healthy adults; reports task-related brain activation results relevant to reappraisal.

Task-based fMRI with 21 healthy participants instructed to use mindfulness and suppression to regulate responses to emotional visual stimuli; reports task-related neural activation (amygdala attenuation and PFC connectivity). This meets I1–I4 and no exclusion criteria apply.

Task-based fMRI study examining cognitive emotion regulation (CER) during aversive Pavlovian conditioning; involves human participants (healthy adult regulators inferred from description of superior/inferior regulators) and reports task-related ventral striatal fMRI activation and modulatory inputs. Meets all inclusion criteria; no exclusion criteria evident.

Task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal of aversive images reporting vlPFC and subcortical activation/pathway analyses. Abstract confirms task-based reappraisal and brain activation but does not explicitly state 'healthy adults', so include for full-text to confirm I3.

Abstract reports a task-based neural study that induced emotions and used cognitive reappraisal to decrease negative affect, and reports neural (amygdala) and self-report outcomes. It does not specify whether stimuli were pictures or explicitly state healthy adult sample, so full text is needed to confirm I3 and picture-based stimuli.

Excluded (E2): study includes only adolescent/delinquent and community adolescent samples—no healthy adult group. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI) and I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I3 (no healthy adult sample) and I2 (no explicit reappraisal/emotion-regulation instructions; task assessed cognitive control/inhibition with socioaffective cues).

Task-based fMRI study examining emotional reactivity and down-regulation in GAD, reporting prefrontal and amygdala engagement — indicating an emotion regulation task and task-related neural activation. The abstract does not specify whether a healthy control group is included, so inclusion on that criterion is uncertain; include for full-text review to confirm.

E2: Study uses resting-state fMRI in children/adolescents and does not include a healthy adult sample. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (not task-based fMRI), I2 (no emotion regulation/reappraisal task), I3 (no healthy adult sample), I4 (no task-related activation reported).

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria I1, I2, I3, and I4 are satisfied (task-based fMRI reported; emotion regulation via distancing/third-person self-talk; healthy adult participants; task-related brain activation reported). However, the study’s fMRI task involved recalling negative autobiographical memories rather than regulating emotional responses to pictures, so it does not address the review objective (fMRI reappraisal of pictures).

Excluded because this is a structural MRI study of cortical gyrification, not a task-based fMRI emotion regulation/reappraisal study. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (includes healthy adult control group). Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation/reappraisal task), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI emotion regulation paradigm in humans, includes both PTSD patients and a healthy control group, and reports task-related activation changes (prefrontal, SMA, VLPFC). All inclusion criteria met; no exclusion criteria apparent.

EXCLUDED: E2 applies — study includes adolescents only (no healthy adult sample). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I2 (no explicit emotion regulation/reappraisal task; it's an emotional attention/distractor task), I3 (no healthy adult group).

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study using reappraisal to regulate responses to social (laughter) stimuli and reports task-related activations (left DLPFC) and connectivity. It does not clearly state inclusion of a healthy control group, so include for full-text review to confirm I3.

Task-based fMRI study with human participants using explicit cognitive reappraisal instructions (Observe/Maintain/Regulate). Includes a healthy normal-weight control group and reports task-related brain activation and connectivity results. No exclusion criteria met.

Task-based fMRI study reporting neural activation during an explicit emotion regulation (ER) task in a sample of healthy adults (n=60). Abstract lacks detail about whether regulation used reappraisal specifically and whether stimuli were pictures, so include for full-text review to confirm reappraisal and picture-based stimuli.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study examining cognitive reappraisal (and suppression) of negative emotion in human participants, reports task-related brain activation, and includes healthy adult participants—meeting all inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract.

Abstract reports an experimental mood manipulation and neural effects but does not specify task-based fMRI nor that participants performed an explicit reappraisal/emotion-regulation task or report task-related activation. No exclusion criteria are clearly met. Include for full-text review to confirm I1–I4.

The study uses resting-state fMRI in mTBI patients and controls and does not report a task-based emotion regulation/reappraisal paradigm or task-related activation. It includes healthy controls (I3) but fails to meet I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation/reappraisal task), and I4 (task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria are met.

Study reports a task-based fMRI paradigm where participants used reappraisal (vs acceptance and no-regulation) while viewing sad images; includes a healthy control group and reports task-related brain activation. Therefore it meets I1–I4 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Abstract reports task-based fMRI comparing placebo and cognitive reappraisal with reappraisal-related activations and decreased amygdala/insula activity, satisfying I1, I2, and I4. The abstract does not specify whether participants were healthy adults (I3 unclear). Include for full-text review to confirm sample; no exclusions evident.

Abstract reports intrinsic brain activity/connectivity (resting-state) related to obesity, not a task-based fMRI reappraisal/emotion-regulation study and does not report task-related activations. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation/reappraisal task), I4 (task-related activation results); I3 (healthy adult sample) not demonstrated.

Included for full-text review: abstract investigates emotion regulation neural correlates and includes unaffected/low-risk healthy adult twin groups (meets I3). Abstract does not specify task-based fMRI, explicit reappraisal instructions, use of pictures, or clear task-related activation reporting (I1, I2, I4 not demonstrated). Insufficient information to determine inclusion from abstract alone.

Study uses resting-state functional connectivity rather than a task-based fMRI reappraisal/emotion-regulation paradigm. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (not task-based fMRI), I2 (no emotion regulation/reappraisal task), I4 (no task-related activation reported). I3 (healthy control sample) not demonstrated in abstract. High confidence the study does not meet inclusion criteria.

EXCLUDED because abstract does not describe an emotion regulation/reappraisal task instructing participants to regulate their emotional responses to pictures (I2 not met). It is a neuroimaging data descriptor of DMN tasks and neurofeedback with healthy adults. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy adult sample), I4 (reports task-related activation). No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract indicates a neuroimaging study investigating volitional emotion regulation in PTSD, but it does not specify use of reappraisal on pictures, explicit fMRI modality, or whether healthy control group is included. Insufficient detail to confirm all inclusion criteria, so include for full-text review.

Abstract does not describe participants engaging in emotion regulation or reappraisal; stimuli were task-irrelevant and processed unintentionally. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy control group present), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met: I2 (no explicit emotion regulation/reappraisal instructions). No exclusion criteria appear to be met.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in which adult participants used cognitive reappraisal to regulate responses to negative and neutral pictures, includes healthy adults (n=54), and reports reappraisal-related brain activation results. No exclusion criteria are met.

Task-based fMRI with healthy adult participants (23 F, 20 M) who explicitly performed cognitive downregulation of negative/stressful sensations (reappraisal-like) during a psychosocial stress task; reports task-related brain activation results. All inclusion criteria I1–I4 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

Abstract is too brief/unspecified about methods: it does not state whether this is task-based fMRI, whether participants performed a reappraisal/emotion-regulation task, participant characteristics, or task-related brain activation results. No exclusion criteria are clearly met. Include for full-text review to determine eligibility.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal (CR) and attention deployment to down-regulate negative emotion, includes 18 presumably healthy adult participants, and reports task-related brain activation (PFC and amygdala). All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

No task was used: this is a resting-state functional connectivity study correlating trait emotion regulation with amygdala connectivity, not a task-based reappraisal/ER experiment. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (not task-based fMRI), I2 (no emotion regulation/reappraisal task performed), I4 (reports resting-state connectivity, not task-related activation).

Abstract reports task-based fMRI in healthy police recruits with task-related aPFC–amygdala activation during control of emotional actions. However, it does not specify use of reappraisal strategies or regulation of responses to pictures, so eligibility for the reappraisal-picture meta-analysis is unclear. Full-text review needed.

Excluded because the study used fNIRS (PFC oxygenation) rather than task-based fMRI, so I1 (task-based fMRI) is not met. The study does not involve participants regulating their own emotional responses or using reappraisal (I2 not met). It is a task-based fMRI study with healthy adult participants and reports task-related activations (I1, I3, I4 met). No exclusion criteria E1–E3 apply.

Task-based perfusion MRI study reporting task-related brain activation during spontaneous vs instructed avoidance of negative emotional material in healthy adults. It does satisfy I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (cognitive reappraisal emotion-regulation task), and I4 (reports task-related functional connectivity results), but does not meet I3 (no healthy adult sample reported).

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI; participants performed reappraisal to increase/reduce emotional responses to pictures; includes healthy control group; reports task-related brain activation results. No exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract.

Abstract indicates use of simultaneous EEG-fMRI to investigate neural activity under cognitive reappraisal, suggesting relevance to emotion regulation. However the abstract does not report participants (human/healthy), task details (pictures), or task-related activation results. Insufficient information to confirm all inclusion criteria, so include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI study that explicitly includes a reappraisal (intentional emotion regulation) task and reports task-related brain activation (amygdala, IFG connectivity). The abstract does not specify stimulus type (pictures) or explicitly state participants were healthy adults, so include for full-text to confirm stimuli and sample health status.

Study examines fMRI responses to perceived controllability of pain and coping, not an emotion regulation/reappraisal task involving regulation of emotional responses to pictures. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy adults), I4 (reports task-related activations). Inclusion not met: I2 (no explicit emotion regulation or reappraisal task). No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (an emotion regulation task), describes neural activation and overlap findings, and implies healthy adult participants. It meets inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are indicated in the abstract.

Excluded because the abstract does not describe participants performing an explicit emotion regulation or reappraisal task (I2 not met). The study is a task-based fMRI study (I1), includes a healthy control group (non-FHR participants; I3), and reports task-related brain activation results (I4). No exclusion criteria (E1-E3) are clearly met based on the abstract.

Abstract indicates neurobiological investigation and ACC activation in older adults but does not specify that participants performed a reappraisal emotion-regulation task with pictures. Insufficient information to confirm inclusion criteria I1–I4 from abstract alone, so include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI study where participants used reappraisal (and distraction) to regulate emotions to pictures; includes remitted depression patients and healthy controls; reports task-related neural activation (amygdala, ACC, OFC). All inclusion criteria met and no exclusion criteria apparent.

Excluded because the abstract reports passive viewing of emotional video clips without instruction to regulate or reappraise, so inclusion criterion I2 (emotion regulation/reappraisal task) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy adult sample), I4 (reports task-related activation). Exclusion criteria met: none (E1–E3 not clearly applicable).

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion met: I3 (study includes war veterans with and without PTSD, i.e., a healthy control group). Not met: I1 (resting-state fMRI, not task-based), I2 (no emotion regulation/reappraisal task described), I4 (reports resting-state connectivity, not task-related activation).

Study used resting-state fMRI to examine amygdala-centered RSFC and habitual (self-reported) reappraisal, not a task-based emotion regulation/reappraisal paradigm with participants regulating responses to pictures; therefore inclusion criteria I1, I2, and I4 are not met. Inclusion met: I3 (healthy adults). No exclusion criteria were met.

Task-based fMRI study using antecedent descriptions as an extrinsic/incidental reappraisal to attenuate emotional responses to unpleasant pictures; reports modulation of amygdala and insula (task-related activations). Abstract does not explicitly state the participant sample as healthy adults, so include for full-text review to confirm I3.

Excluded because this is a structural morphometry study, not a task-based fMRI investigation of emotion regulation or reappraisal. Includes healthy adults (I3) but does not involve an emotion regulation/reappraisal task (I2), is not task-based fMRI (I1), and does not report task-related brain activation (I4). No exclusion criteria met.

No exclusion criteria met. Satisfies I1 (task-based event-related fMRI), I3 (healthy adult sample: healthy women), and I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Does NOT meet I2: participants did not perform an emotion regulation/reappraisal task; study manipulated DLPFC with HF-rTMS and examined attentional processing of emotional stimuli rather than instructing reappraisal/regulation of their own emotions.

Abstract describes task-based fMRI with task-related activation (I1, I4 met) but does not indicate inclusion of a healthy adult control group and does not describe an emotion reappraisal/regulation instruction to increase/decrease own emotions. Excluding due to E2 (no healthy adult sample).

Exclusion based on failure to meet I2: the study is a yoked Pavlovian fear-conditioning fMRI experiment manipulating predictability and controllability of aversive stimuli; participants were not instructed to use reappraisal or other explicit emotion-regulation strategies to regulate their responses to pictures. Inclusion criteria met: I1, I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I2. Exclusion criteria met: none (no E1–E3 applicable).

EXCLUDED: While this is a task-based fMRI study (I1) of healthy adults (I3) reporting task-related activations (I4), the task was an implicit emotion-processing gender-discrimination task with no instruction to regulate or reappraise emotions; therefore I2 (emotion regulation/reappraisal) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E1–E3) apply.

Task-based fMRI study using personalized in-scanner worry induction and reappraisal; includes both late-life GAD and non-anxious (healthy) participants; reports task-related cerebral blood flow activation results across conditions. Meets inclusion criteria I1–I4; no exclusion criteria met.

Study is task-based fMRI with healthy controls and reports task-related activation (I1, I3, I4 met). However, the task involved incidental emotional processing during a gender-discrimination task with no instructions to regulate or reappraise emotions, so it does not meet I2 (emotion regulation/reappraisal). No exclusion criteria met.

Excluded because the study used resting-state fMRI and baseline HRV correlations, not a task-based emotion regulation/reappraisal paradigm. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (healthy adult samples). Inclusion not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation/reappraisal task), I4 (task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria met.

Task-based fMRI with a validated emotion regulation task in drug-naïve IGD youth and matched healthy controls; reports task-related neural activation differences. Abstract does not specify whether the regulation strategy was reappraisal or whether stimuli were pictures, so full-text review is needed to confirm those specifics.

Excluded because the study used resting-state fMRI of a meditation intervention in depressed patients rather than a task-based reappraisal emotion-regulation paradigm. Exclusion met: E2 (no healthy adult sample reported). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (not task-based), I2 (not an emotion-regulation/reappraisal task), I3 (no healthy control reported), I4 (no task-related activations).

Excluded (E2): resting-state fMRI study in adolescent girls with no healthy adult sample. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (not task-based), I2 (no emotion regulation/reappraisal task), I3 (no healthy adult group), I4 (no task-related activation reported).

Task-based fMRI with explicit instruction to up-regulate emotions to images (increase emotion). Sample: 63 healthy young adults. Reports task-related brain activation (ventral striatum). Therefore I1, I2, I3, and I4 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria met.

Abstract does not provide sufficient information to determine whether this is a task-based fMRI study of voluntary emotion regulation (reappraisal), or whether healthy control participants were included. Inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone, so include for full-text review.

Study is a task-based fMRI of Zen meditation using a thermal pain paradigm, not an emotion-reappraisal of pictures. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy adult sample), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met: I2 (does not involve participants regulating their own emotional responses to pictures via reappraisal; meditation/pain paradigm is different). No exclusion criteria from list are triggered (none met).

Study used resting-state fMRI (no task), and did not involve participants regulating their emotional responses to pictures using reappraisal; it reports intrinsic connectivity, not task-related activation. Includes healthy adults (I3). Does not meet I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation/reappraisal task), or I4 (task-related activation results).

I2 not met: study did not instruct participants to regulate or reappraise emotions; they passively viewed fearful vs neutral faces under ketamine. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy adult sample), I4 (reports task-related activation). Exclusion criteria met: none.

Meets inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI (I1); participants performed an emotion regulation task (distraction) during picture symptom provocation (I2); includes healthy control group (I3); reports task-related BOLD activation results (I4). No exclusion criteria met. Although the strategy is distraction rather than reappraisal, the inclusion criteria allow broad emotion regulation; include for full-text review to confirm eligibility for a reappraisal-specific meta-analysis.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation paradigm in which participants were instructed to increase positive emotion (explicit regulation). Includes a healthy comparison group and reports task-related brain activation/connectivity results (nucleus accumbens, fronto-striatal). No exclusion criteria met.

Task-based fMRI with instructed regulation of negative emotion in 55 healthy participants and whole-brain activation reported. These satisfy I1, I2, I3, I4. Abstract does not specify whether regulation used reappraisal specifically or whether stimuli were pictures, so full-text review is needed to confirm those details.

Study is task-based fMRI and reports task-related activations (I1, I4). However, it includes only bipolar disorder patients with no healthy adult control group (meets exclusion E2) and does not describe an instructed emotion-regulation or reappraisal task (I2 not met). Exclude based on E2.

Task-based fMRI with 42 human participants instructed to prepare and then use reappraisal (and suppression) in response to negative, high-arousing images; reports task-related brain activation. All inclusion criteria met; no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded (E2): sample consists of children only (ages 7-11); no healthy adult sample. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI) and I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I2 (no emotion regulation/reappraisal instructions; task was perceptual judgments of faces) and I3 (no healthy adult group).

Excluded because the study did not involve participants regulating their own emotions via reappraisal. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy adults), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met: I2 (no emotion-regulation/reappraisal instruction). No exclusion criteria met (none).

E3: Empathy/perspective-taking study without explicit instructions to amplify/attenuate participants' own emotions. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy adults), I4 (reports task-related brain activation/connectivity). Inclusion not met: I2 (no evidence of an emotion-regulation or reappraisal instruction).

Excluded because inclusion criterion I2 (explicit emotion regulation/reappraisal task) is not met: the study used an affective Stroop with emotional distracters, not instructed reappraisal. Inclusion criteria met: I1, I3, I4. No exclusion criteria clearly met.

Excluded because abstract describes only VCFS patients and does not include a healthy adult control group (E2). No emotion regulation or reappraisal task is described (I2 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy adult sample), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria (E1–E3) are met.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of social decision-making (trust game) in female MDD patients and controls. It meets I1, I3, and I4, but does not involve participants regulating their own emotional responses to pictures using reappraisal or instructions to increase/decrease emotion (I2 not met). No exclusion criteria are specifically met.

Study examines nocebo responses via classical conditioning in visceral pain, not emotion regulation/reappraisal. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I2 (no reappraisal/emotion regulation task), I1 (task-based fMRI not clearly reported), I3 (healthy adults not specified), I4 (task-related brain activation results not reported).

Study is resting-state fMRI, not a task-based emotion regulation/reappraisal paradigm. Inclusion met: I3 (includes healthy control group). Inclusion not met: I1 (not task-based fMRI), I2 (participants did not perform emotion regulation/reappraisal), I4 (no task-related activation reported). No exclusion criteria (E1-E3) are met.

E1: Abstract describes a conceptual/model paper and does not report original human data. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performing reappraisal/emotion regulation), I3 (healthy adult sample), I4 (task-related brain activation results).

Study is a resting-state fMRI connectivity study and does not involve a task-based emotion regulation or reappraisal paradigm nor report task-related activations. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (includes healthy control group). Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performing emotion regulation/reappraisal), I4 (task-related brain activation results).

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy adult sample), I4 (task-related brain activation reported). Inclusion not met: I2 — abstract does not describe participants regulating their own emotional responses or using reappraisal; it reports passive angry-face processing and effects of mindfulness training.

Excluded because the study does not include a healthy adult sample (E2). It is a task-based fMRI study (I1), uses an emotion regulation task in human adolescents (I2), and reports task-related neural results (functional connectivity; I4). However, it only includes adolescent participants (no adult healthy group), so I3 is not met.

Task-based fMRI study of 54 healthy adults using reappraisal to volitionally regulate emotions; reports task-related alterations in functional connectivity during reappraisal vs maintain. Meets I1–I4. No exclusion criteria apparent from abstract.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I1) with healthy adult participants (I3) reporting task-related brain activation (I4). However, participants were not instructed to regulate their own emotional responses via reappraisal—the manipulation was an aversive gustatory aftertaste paired with images, not a cognitive reappraisal task. Therefore I2 (reappraisal/emotion-regulation task) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E1–E3) are triggered.

Abstract describes neurostimulation and reward-circuit connectivity in depressed patients; it does not report a task-based fMRI reappraisal/emotion-regulation paradigm or inclusion of healthy adult controls. Exclusion E2 applies. Inclusion criteria I1–I4 are not demonstrated in the abstract.

Excluded because E2: study does not include a healthy adult sample. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (not an emotion regulation/reappraisal task; social exclusion task), I3 (no healthy adult group; participants are adolescents ages 11-17).

Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (includes a healthy adult control group). E2 met: study sample are youth (BP-I and BP-NOS) with healthy youth controls, not healthy adults. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met or not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI not clearly specified in abstract), I2 (no explicit reappraisal/emotion-regulation task described), I3 (no healthy adult sample), I4 (task-related activation results not clearly reported).

Task-based fMRI study where human participants (lean to obese adults) used cognitive reappraisal strategies to regulate food craving; reports neural responsivity results. Meets inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI, reappraisal task, healthy adult sample, and task-related brain activation. No exclusion criteria apparent from abstract.

Excluded because the study examines neural correlates of nostalgia evoked by music, not participants actively regulating their emotional responses via reappraisal. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I2 (no emotion regulation/reappraisal task evident), I3 (healthy adult sample not explicitly demonstrated in abstract).

Abstract describes a methodological fMRI model applied to data from a study of socially mediated emotion regulation but does not specify that participants performed reappraisal of pictures or report task-related activation. Insufficient information to determine if inclusion criteria I2 and I4 are met; include for full-text review.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study—voxel-based morphometry structural MRI), I2 (no emotion regulation/reappraisal task reported), I4 (no task-related activation results reported), I3 not demonstrated (no healthy control group mentioned). Title/abstract indicate a structural study of depressed outpatients, so exclude.

Task-based fMRI study with healthy older adult participants performing an explicit reappraisal task (increase/maintain/decrease) in response to unpleasant pictures; reports task-related BOLD activation results. Meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are met.

Study is a decision-making fMRI investigation of second-order uncertainty/ambiguity, not an emotion regulation/reappraisal task. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I2 (does not involve participants regulating their emotional responses via reappraisal of pictures), I3 (abstract does not specify a healthy adult sample).

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study using a cognitive reappraisal paradigm in non-medicated depressed youth and healthy controls, with task-related neural activation results (amygdala, vmPFC). All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded: this is a structural MRI (voxel-based morphometry) study, not a task-based fMRI emotion regulation/reappraisal study. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (healthy adults). Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation/reappraisal task), I4 (task-related activation results).

Study applies reappraisal to monetary reward anticipation (monetary cues), not to emotional responses elicited by pictures as required by the review objective. Inclusion met: I1, I2, I3, I4. Excluded because the study does not include an explicit emotion regulation/reappraisal task (I2 not met) and does not include healthy adults (participants are youth; I3 not met), meeting exclusion E2. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI) and I4 (reports task-related activation). Exclusion criteria applied: E2 (no healthy adult sample).

EXCLUDED: Structural imaging study of hippocampal cell density in healthy adults; not a task-based fMRI study, does not involve an emotion regulation/reappraisal task, and does not report task-related brain activation. Inclusion met: I3. Inclusion not met: I1, I2, I4. No exclusion criteria met.

Study is a structural MRI surface morphometry study, not a task-based fMRI emotion regulation/reappraisal study. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (includes healthy control group). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not task-based fMRI), I2 (no emotion regulation/reappraisal task), I4 (no task-related brain activation reported). No exclusion criteria are met.

E1 met: Abstract is a conceptual/theoretical paper proposing fMRI neurofeedback without original human data. Inclusion criteria met: none. Study is a task-based fMRI of emotional face processing without any instruction to regulate or reappraise emotions. No evidence of a reappraisal/emotion-regulation task. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion met: I1, I3, I4. Inclusion not met: I2 (no reappraisal/regulation task).

Excluded because study used resting-state fMRI rather than task-based fMRI (I1 not met); no emotion regulation/reappraisal task reported (I2 not met); no task-related activation results reported (I4 not met); presence of a healthy control group is not stated (I3 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria (E1-E3) explicitly met.

Abstract indicates an fMRI task involving viewing emotional/risk-taking actions but does not state participants used reappraisal or explicit emotion-regulation instructions. E3 met — the task is self/ideal/avatar reflection without instructions to regulate (increase/decrease) emotion or use reappraisal. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (includes healthy controls), I4 (reports task-related activations). Inclusion not met: I2 (no emotion-regulation/reappraisal task).

Task-based fMRI with romantically involved (presumably healthy) adults and reports task-related neural activation during implicit derogation of attractive alternatives. Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (includes healthy adult control group). Excluded: abstract does not describe a task-based fMRI reappraisal emotion-regulation task. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Excluded: abstract does not describe an explicit emotion regulation or reappraisal task (I2 not met). It is a task-based fMRI study of motivated reasoning with healthy adult participants and reports task activations (I1, I3, I4 met). No exclusion criteria clearly met.

The study reports associative emotional learning (not instructed emotion regulation/reappraisal). Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I4 (reports task-related activation). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I2 (no evidence of reappraisal/regulation task), I3 (participant health status not specified as healthy adults). No exclusion criteria clearly apply.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in which human participants performed positive and minimizing reappraisal to regulate emotional responses to negative stimuli; reports task-related brain activations (amygdala, ventral striatum, vmPFC) and connectivity. Excluded for E2: no healthy adult sample (participants are adolescents). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Excluded because the study does not involve an emotion regulation/reappraisal task (I2 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy adult sample), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria met (none of E1–E3 apply). Study does not involve participants regulating their own emotional responses to pictures using reappraisal; it manipulates cognitive load while inducing anticipatory anxiety, indexing appraisal processes but not explicit emotion regulation/reappraisal instruction. Appears to be a task-based fMRI study with healthy adults reporting task-related brain activation (I1,I3,I4 satisfied), but I2 not met. No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract clearly studies cognitive reappraisal and links prefrontal engagement to neural activity and inflammation, indicating task-related brain activation during reappraisal (satisfies I2 and I4). The abstract does not explicitly state use of task-based fMRI (I1) nor clearly report inclusion of healthy adult participants (I3). Insufficient detail to exclude; include for full-text review to confirm I1 and I3.

No evidence of an emotion regulation/reappraisal instruction — study examined perception of emotional faces (I2 not met). Abstract does not demonstrate inclusion of a healthy adult control group (I3 not demonstrated). It is a task-based fMRI study reporting task-related activation (I1 and I4 satisfied). No exclusion criteria from E1–E3 are clearly met.

Not a task-based fMRI study (I1 not met): this is an EEG/ERP (LPP) study. Includes healthy adults (I3 met) and reports task-related brain activation measures (I4 met). No exclusion criteria (E1–E3) apply.

No evidence participants were instructed to regulate their own emotions via reappraisal or analogous strategies (I2 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI) and I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not demonstrated: I2 (explicit emotion regulation/reappraisal task) and I3 (healthy adult sample not explicitly stated). No exclusion criteria clearly met (exclusion IDs: []).

No evidence participants were instructed to regulate their own emotions using reappraisal (I2 not met). No exclusion criteria clearly met. Excluded because the abstract reports passive fMRI responses to negative faces with genotyping but does not describe any emotion regulation or reappraisal instructions. EXCLUDED: The study used structural MRI (voxel-based morphometry), not a task-based fMRI emotion regulation/reappraisal paradigm. Exclusion IDs met: none. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy adult groups), I4 (reports task-related brain activation/connectivity). Abstract does not indicate participants performed an explicit emotion regulation/reappraisal task; it examines brain responses related to empathy/emotions in healthy nulliparous young-adult women. Excluded because this is a diffusion tensor imaging (structural) study in euthymic bipolar patients, not a task-based fMRI reappraisal study. No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion: I3 (study includes healthy adult participants). Abstract describes a Go/No-Go task with negative feedback in remitted MDD, not an emotion regulation/reappraisal task. Abstract reports diffusion MRI/structural connectivity in bipolar disorder, not a task-based fMRI study examining emotion regulation/reappraisal; it does not report task-related brain activation. Includes healthy controls (I3). Inclusion criteria not met: I1, I2, I4. No exclusion criteria met.

Excluded because the study does not involve participants regulating their emotional responses via reappraisal (I2 not met). Abstract describes a stress-induction task, not an emotion-regulation reappraisal task.

No evidence participants performed emotion regulation/reappraisal. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (includes healthy controls), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met: I2 (not an emotion regulation/reappraisal task). No exclusion criteria met.

Study is resting-state fMRI, not a task-based emotion regulation/reappraisal study. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (healthy adult participants). Task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (down-regulation) in N=20 healthy adults reporting task-related brain activation (prefrontal and amygdala correlations). Fits all inclusion criteria.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in which human participants were instructed to use reappraisal (increase positive/decrease negative) while viewing negative pictures and reports task-related brain activation (amygdala, thalamus, midbrain). Not a task-based fMRI study (EEG study measuring LPP), so I1 (task-based fMRI) is not met. Inclusion met: I2 (uses reappraisal/distraction emotion regulation), I4 (reports task-related brain activation - EEG LPP). I3 (healthy adult sample) not demonstrated in abstract. Abstract shows instructed increase/decrease emotion to pictures (I2 met). Inclusion I3 (healthy adult sample) is not demonstrated in the abstract. No exclusion criteria applied.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (includes healthy control group), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (does not assess emotion regulation or reappraisal; uses a cognitive interference MSIT task with no instruction to regulate emotional responses to pictures).

Abstract reports task-based fMRI of conscious regulation of negative autobiographical memories in MDD patients (meets I1, I2, I4). It does not report inclusion of healthy adult controls (E2 applies). Also it uses autobiographical memory regulation rather than reappraisal of pictures, so it does not address the review objective.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study examining the effect of escitalopram on emotion regulation of negative stimuli, indicating an emotion regulation task; however the abstract does not state whether participants were healthy adults nor explicitly report task-related activation results, so full-text is needed to confirm I3 and I4.

Exclusion criteria met: E2 (no healthy adult sample—participants are adolescents) and E3 (study probes empathy/perspective-taking without explicit instruction to up-/down-regulate one’s own emotion). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI) and I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not met or not demonstrated: I2 (no clear emotion-regulation/reappraisal task instruction) and I3 (no healthy adult group).

Excluded (E1): this is a study protocol without original human data. Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (no evidence of task-based fMRI), I2 (no evidence of participants performing emotion regulation/reappraisal), I3 (no healthy control group reported), I4 (no task-related brain activation results reported).

Abstract investigates neural correlates of emotion regulation and includes nonpatient controls, but does not specify that this is a task-based fMRI study involving participant reappraisal of pictures or report task-related activation. Excluded because the study is not a task-based fMRI study (I1 not met) and does not involve an emotion regulation/reappraisal task (I2 not met). Abstract only states a 'controlled fMRI study' of MBCT in bipolar disorder but gives no details about a task-based emotion regulation (reappraisal) paradigm, use of emotional pictures, or inclusion of a healthy control group. E1: Abstract describes a review/theoretical overview without original task-based fMRI data. Does not report human participants performing reappraisal or task-related activation. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1, I2, I3, I4.

Excluded (E2): study includes only patients with social anxiety disorder; no healthy adult control group. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task—attention deployment), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (no healthy adult sample).

Abstract reports neural activity to tasks involving emotional stimuli but does not specify that participants used reappraisal/emotion-regulation strategies or explicitly that the imaging was task-based fMRI. Insufficient detail to confirm I1-I3, so include for full-text review to determine whether reappraisal and healthy adult sample are present.

No task-based fMRI: this is an ERP (LPP) study, so I1 not met. The abstract does report neural responses (LPP), so I4 is met. Presence of healthy adults (I3) is not demonstrated in the abstract. No exclusion criteria (E1–E3) are clearly met.

The study reports task-based fMRI examining emotional reactivity and top-down regulation in 60 women with BPD but does not report any healthy control group. Exclusion criterion met: E2 (no healthy adult sample). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met: I3 (no healthy control group reported).

EXCLUDE — E3 met: this is an empathy/perspective-taking task without explicit instruction to regulate one's own emotion. Inclusion met: I4 (reports task-related brain activation via fNIRS). Excluded because the task involves perspective-taking/empathy instructions (e.g., 'Your-Baby'/'Self') without any explicit instruction to amplify or attenuate the participant's own emotional response (E3). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (includes healthy controls), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Abstract describes diffusion/microstructural correlations between uncinate fasciculus integrity and trait reappraisal in healthy adults, not a task-based fMRI reappraisal experiment. Abstract does not specify use of a task-based fMRI reappraisal/emotion-regulation task or inclusion of healthy control participants; study appears to concern neurofunctional effects of quetiapine in bipolar patients but details are insufficient. Excluded (E2): sample includes only children (8–13), no healthy adult participants. Inclusion criteria met: none. EXCLUDED because the study uses a fear conditioning/extinction paradigm without explicit emotion regulation or reappraisal instructions (I2 not met). Excluding because inclusion criterion I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation/reappraisal task) is not demonstrated in the abstract. Excluded because the study used EEG/ERP (LPP) measures, not task-based fMRI, so inclusion criterion I1 is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (emotion regulation task—suppression), I3 (healthy adult groups), I4 (reports task-related brain activation via ERP). No exclusion criteria clearly met.

Task-based fMRI with explicit emotion regulation instructions (maintain/enhance/suppress) in human participants; includes healthy control group and reports task-related neural activation. No exclusion criteria met.

EXCLUDE because study is EEG/ERP (LPP), not a task-based fMRI study (I1 not met). Exclusion IDs met: none. Study used structural (anatomical) MRI measuring insula volume and trait measures, not a task-based fMRI reappraisal task. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (healthy adult sample). No evidence this is a task-based fMRI study (I1 not met) nor an emotion regulation/reappraisal task (I2 not met). The abstract reports EEG brain responses (Ne/ERN), so I4 is met. Inclusion of healthy adult sample is not demonstrated (I3 not shown). No exclusion criteria (E1–E3) are met.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in which participants were instructed to cognitively reappraise positive and negative images, with reported brain activation differences by condition; no patient population is mentioned so healthy participants are presumed. No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (healthy adult sample present), I4 (reports task-related brain activation via ERPs). Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study includes healthy older adults). Excluded because the study used autobiographical memory recall rather than picture stimuli required by the review objective. Exclusion E2 met: abstract reports fMRI in OCD patients but does not indicate any healthy adult control group. Inclusion criteria met: none. Exclude: No evidence this is a task-based fMRI reappraisal study. Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (reports task-related electrocortical/brain activity). Excluded: the study reports structural morphometry (grey matter volume) associations with habitual reappraisal, not task-based fMRI activation during an emotion-regulation/reappraisal task. Abstract indicates a task-based functional imaging study of emotion regulation but does not specify use of reappraisal, whether healthy controls were included, or explicit task-related activation results. E2: Non-human animal study (adult Lampetra planeri); no human participants and thus no healthy adult sample. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (human emotion regulation/reappraisal), I3 (healthy adult sample), I4 (task-related brain activation).

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion met: I4 (reports task-related neural/EEG results). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study; uses EEG/SEPs), I2 (not an emotion regulation/reappraisal task), I3 (healthy adult sample not specified). Therefore exclude.

Not a task-based fMRI study and does not involve emotion regulation/reappraisal. The study used EEG to examine brain–heart coupling during a gambling feedback task, so it fails key inclusion criteria for this fMRI reappraisal review.

Non-human macaque tracer study; does not include healthy adult human participants (E2). Inclusion criteria met: none. E1: Article is a non-empirical/theoretical paper (Medical Hypotheses) with no original human data. Inclusion criteria not demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study), I2 (no emotion regulation/reappraisal task), I3 (no healthy adult sample), I4 (no task-related brain activation results).

Excluded for E2 (no healthy adult sample). The study is an fMRI task in pigs (I1) and reports task-related brain activation (I4), but does not involve human participants performing emotion regulation/reappraisal (I2) and does not include a healthy adult sample (I3).

Excluded because the study uses resting-state fMRI rather than a task-based emotion regulation/reappraisal paradigm and does not report task-related activations. Excluded because E2: the study does not include a healthy adult control group. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (explicit emotion regulation via distancing), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (no healthy control group reported in abstract).

Excluded due to E2: study does not include a healthy adult sample. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I4 (reports task-related brain activation).
